activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

feedback.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(A)=-63.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{2}{9}{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\frac{2}{9}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =\frac{2}{9}det(A) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}\cdot (-63) \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$
